cases.name: b3.complex.arithmetic
cases.notes: written from the definitions rather than std::complex, whose division and abs branch on magnitudes -- which a hypercomplex AD scalar cannot tolerate
cases.reference: addition, multiplication and division against hand-computed values; (a/b)*b = a; a conj(a) is real and equals |a|^2

cases.expected_description: |A - A^T| = 0 and |A - A^dagger| > 0
cases.name: b3.complex.transpose_and_adjoint_are_distinct
cases.notes: Lorentz reciprocity is the UNCONJUGATED transpose and passivity is the conjugate one. Using the adjoint for reciprocity is a physics error that only appears once the medium is lossy -- which is where B3 begins
cases.reference: for a complex symmetric matrix the plain transpose residual vanishes while the Hermitian adjoint residual does not

cases.name: b3.complex.matrix_inverse_roundtrip
cases.reference: A A^-1 = I for a complex 3x3

cases.name: b3.complex.real_limit_recovery
cases.notes: the imaginary parts are exactly zero, not small: a lossless model must not leak loss through the arithmetic
cases.reference: with every damping set to zero the response is exactly real and matches the undamped closed form

cases.computed_description: kernel exp(-i*omega*t); min Im(Lorentz) over band = 5.6073e-03; Im(Drude) at w=1 = 1.4257e-01
cases.expected_description: Im > 0 for the Lorentz term across the band and for the Drude term
cases.name: b3.convention.sign_of_loss_is_pinned
cases.notes: this is the check that fixes the Fourier convention rather than assuming it. Every passivity sign downstream depends on it
cases.reference: under the recorded e^{-i omega t} kernel both specified model forms have STRICTLY POSITIVE imaginary part for positive parameters, which is passive; under the opposite kernel both would be gain

cases.name: b3.convention.recorded
cases.reference: the Fourier kernel, time derivative, constitutive relation, dissipated power, Poynting vector, passive sign, causal half-plane and reality condition are all recorded

cases.name: b3.dispersion.lorentz_closed_form
cases.reference: the two-pole Lorentz permittivity matches a hand-written closed form

cases.name: b3.dispersion.mu_inverse_is_derived_from_mu
cases.notes: mu is the quantity PARAMETERIZED and mu^-1 is derived by inversion. Parameterizing mu^-1 as a sum of Lorentz terms would place poles of mu^-1 -- zeros of mu -- at the resonances, which is a different and generally non-passive medium
cases.reference: [mu^-1](w) mu(w) = 1 at every sampled frequency

cases.name: b3.dispersion.reality_condition
cases.reference: eps(-w) = conj(eps(w)), the condition for a real time-domain response

cases.name: b3.dispersion.magnetoelectric_is_reciprocal_by_construction
cases.notes: EXACT zero: zeta = z(w) K with K a fixed real antisymmetric shape, so the transpose relation is structural. Independent arbitrary complex entries would break reciprocity by construction and are not used
cases.reference: zeta_adjoint = zeta^T at every frequency, exactly

cases.expected_description: Im(pole) < 0 for all 8 roots
cases.name: b3.causality.poles_in_lower_half_plane
cases.notes: under e^{-i omega t} causality requires analyticity in the UPPER half plane. This is enforced by the parameterization -- gamma is strictly positive by construction -- and not argued from sampled data
cases.reference: every pole of every Lorentz term sits in the LOWER half omega-plane, including the overdamped case where both roots are purely imaginary

cases.expected_description: positive for all inputs
cases.name: b3.causality.positive_transform_is_strictly_positive
cases.notes: this is HARD feasibility for causality: not a penalty that can be traded away, but a parameterization the infeasible region is not in
cases.reference: the damping transform is strictly positive for every input, including extreme negative values, so no optimizer step can produce an acausal model

cases.name: b3.causality.transform_roundtrip
cases.reference: positive_transform(positive_transform_inverse(x)) = x, so a known physical model can be expressed exactly as a design vector

cases.expected_description: monotone decrease with band width, and below 5e-3 on the widest
cases.name: b3.causality.kramers_kronig_diagnostic
cases.notes: A DIAGNOSTIC, NOT the causality proof. A fixed tolerance here would be measuring the principal-value quadrature, not the physics -- which is why the convergence trend is asserted instead. Causality is established structurally by pole placement, and that case is b3.causality.poles_in_lower_half_plane
cases.reference: the Kramers-Kronig residual DECREASES monotonically as the integration band widens, and is small on the widest band -- the signature of quadrature truncation rather than a causality violation

cases.name: b3.passivity.loss_matrix_is_hermitian
cases.notes: Hermitian by construction, so this catches an error in the assembly rather than in the physics
cases.reference: L = (C - C^dagger)/(2i) is Hermitian at every band frequency

cases.name: b3.passivity.reciprocity_in_EH_representation
cases.notes: many references write xi = -zeta^T; that sign traces to the opposite convention for zeta in D = eps E - zeta B. This project's sign was derived at B1C and cross-checked against Minkowski's moving-medium relations, so the relation is verified here rather than imported
cases.reference: xi_EH = zeta_EH^T, the reciprocity relation DERIVED for this project's (E,B) sign convention

cases.expected_description: min eigenvalue of L is 0
cases.name: b3.passivity.vacuum_is_lossless
cases.reference: the nondispersive vacuum limit has loss eigenvalues exactly zero: passive, and on the boundary rather than inside it

cases.expected_description: min eigenvalue of L >= 0 at every frequency
cases.name: b3.passivity.damped_lorentz_is_passive
cases.reference: a damped two-pole Lorentz medium is passive across the whole band: the smallest eigenvalue of the loss matrix is non-negative

cases.computed_description: min loss eigenvalue -2.9630e+00, violation 2.9630e+00, pole Im = 9.0000e-02
cases.expected_description: passivity violated and poles in the upper half plane
cases.name: b3.passivity.active_oscillator_is_rejected
cases.notes: the test must be able to FAIL a medium, or a passing verdict on a passive one means nothing
cases.reference: a Lorentz term with NEGATIVE damping is detected as active -- the loss matrix acquires a negative eigenvalue -- and its poles move into the upper half plane, so it is acausal as well

cases.computed_description: min Im eps = 3.1250e-06, min Im mu = 1.1211e-06, yet min eigenvalue of L = -3.7943e+00 at w = 3.6000e+00
cases.expected_description: positive diagonal imaginary parts, negative loss eigenvalue
cases.name: b3.passivity.diagonal_imaginary_parts_are_not_sufficient
cases.notes: this is why 'all imaginary parts are positive' must NOT be equated with passivity for a coupled bianisotropic medium. The off-diagonal block L_12 = (xi_EH - zeta_EH^dagger)/(2i) carries the coupling, and with near-lossless diagonal blocks it alone sets the spectrum
cases.reference: a medium with STRICTLY POSITIVE Im eps and Im mu at every frequency is nevertheless NOT passive when the magnetoelectric coupling is strong: the full loss matrix has a negative eigenvalue

cases.name: b3.band.a11_is_real_linear
cases.notes: this is what licenses Z(w) = A11(Re blocks) + i A11(Im blocks), so the verified real reconstruction is reused rather than a second complex implementation being written
cases.reference: (A11) is homogeneous linear in the blocks with real coefficients

cases.expected_description: all mismatch measures zero at the target
cases.name: b3.band.zero_at_exact_target_and_reported_separately
cases.notes: the contributions are never collapsed into one number: a model that is excellent at band centre and poor at the edges is a different object from one that is uniformly mediocre
cases.reference: J_band vanishes at the exact target, and the centre, mean and worst frequency mismatches are reported as three distinct numbers

cases.name: b3.gradient.complex_step
cases.notes: the agreement is limited by the CENTRED DIFFERENCE, not by the complex step: the latter has no subtractive cancellation and is exact to machine precision. The scalar seam is what makes this possible without a second implementation
cases.reference: complex-step derivatives, from instantiating the model at Scalar = Complex<double> with a step of 1e-30, agree with centred differences

cases.name: b3.hard_feasible_versus_soft_penalty
cases.notes: B2 admitted a small violation because a smooth hinge trades feasibility for differentiability. Here feasibility comes from a bounded parameter transform plus projection, so it is exact, and a soft result is NEVER called feasible merely because its violation is small
cases.reference: the hard-feasible run satisfies the bound EXACTLY -- zero violation -- and is labelled feasible, while the soft-penalised run is reported under a different name whatever the size of its violation

cases.name: b3.frame_orientation_matters_for_anisotropic_shapes
cases.notes: this is physics, not a defect. The isotropic parts are triad independent -- sum_i e_i^a e_i^b = h^{ab} for any triad -- but an anisotropic shape is not, so transforming the setup means transforming the FRAME, which is what the covariance case above does
cases.reference: the same coefficients on an independently rebuilt triad give a DIFFERENT tensor, because the magnetoelectric shape K singles out particular spatial directions
